name: Tri-State Ready Restoration
what_they_do: Water, fire and mold damage restoration contractor - emergency water extraction and drying, flooded basement and burst-pipe cleanup, sewage cleanup, leak detection, storm damage, plus an insurance-claims service. Site claims over 20 years in the restoration industry and 24/7 emergency response, and advertises across NJ, Philadelphia, NY, California, North Carolina and Florida.
customers: Homeowners and property owners facing insurance-claim emergencies (burst pipes, flooded basements, mold), plus referrals from insurers and agents.

size_signals.signal: 'Over 20 years of experience in the restoration industry' stated on the home page; ~20+ service pages, FAQ pages and a blog
Single Spotswood address (213 Summerhill Road); no crew photos, team page or truck photos found on the home page

listing.platform: Porch profile (no ratings shown); no Google rating surfaced in searches

website_review.primary_cta: 'Call Now (908) 417-7980' in the header plus a free-estimate form on the home page and a 'free estimate' link to the contact page
website_review.online_booking_or_quote: Forminator quote form on the home page (Name, Email, Address, Phone, Service dropdown, message) and another on the contact page; no CAPTCHA; no calendar booking
website_review.trust_signals: 20+ years claimed, 24/7 availability, service-specific FAQ pages, insurance-claims page, blog, service dropdown
website_review.out_of_date_signs: Broken contact details: the email on the page renders as 'tri-statereadyrestoration.com' with no @ and no mailbox; the tel: href contains spaces ('tel: +1 908 417 7980'), which some phones will not dial; the home form collects the email field twice; no photography of actual crews or jobs anywhere
website_review.search_basics: Title and description name water/fire/mold restoration and the served states but not Spotswood or any town; service pages exist for each damage type; copy says California, North Carolina and Florida as well, which dilutes the local claim
top_issues: No LocalBusiness schema - the JSON-LD graph is only WebPage / ImageObject / BreadcrumbList / WebSite / Organization, so address, phone, hours and services are not machine-readable
No real reviews: no Google rating found, and the only testimonials are self-published on the site
Broken contact data (malformed email address, tel: href with spaces) and a duplicated email field on the home form
Hero headline is enormous on mobile - on a 390px screen the H1 alone fills more than a full viewport before any offer or form is visible
No response-time promise in text (e.g. 'on site within X hours') and no service-area town list, both of which insurance-driven buyers ask for first

agent_readiness.notes: Findable: robots.txt is fully open (Allow: /, no disallowed paths) so OAI-SearchBot, PerplexityBot and Googlebot are allowed; sitemap_index.xml present; but no Google listing rating was found, so profile completeness is unknown. Answerable: services, states served, 24/7 availability and 20+ years are real text and FAQs exist, yet there is no LocalBusiness/Service schema, no hours pattern, no price or insurance-deductible guidance. Bookable: the labelled Forminator form (Name, Email, Address, Phone, Service, message) works without CAPTCHA, but the email/phone links are malformed and there is no scheduling - and for emergency work a form is weak.

operations_signals.signal: 24/7 emergency line plus insurance-claims handling means after-hours triage, job intake and documentation are staff-heavy (inference from the service model)
Separate FAQ pages for water, fire and mold restoration - staff are repeatedly answering the same questions

top_opportunities.opportunity: Emergency intake agent: answer after-hours calls and form submissions, triage water vs fire vs mold, capture address and insurance details, and dispatch with a quoted response window
top_opportunities.evidence: Site advertises 24/7 response, an insurance-claims workflow and a generic quote form; no on-call triage layer visible

top_opportunities.opportunity: Fix trust basics: verified Google Business Profile with job photos and review requests, fix the broken email and tel: links, add LocalBusiness schema with address, hours and service area
top_opportunities.evidence: No Google rating found in searches; email renders without @; tel: href contains spaces; JSON-LD has no LocalBusiness node

top_opportunities.opportunity: Compress the mobile hero and lead with '24/7 water damage - call now / get help in 60 seconds' plus a click-to-call band, so the phone CTA is visible without scrolling
top_opportunities.evidence: 390px screenshot shows the H1 ('Restoration Services in New Jersey, Philadelphia, New York, California, North Carolina & Florida...') consuming the entire first viewport

scores.reasons: Gap: good service-page structure undermined by no schema, no reviews, broken contact data and a mobile hero that buries the offer. Pay: restoration jobs are high-ticket ($5k-$50k insurance work) but the operation looks small and single-address. Ease: schema, links and mobile hero are quick wins; the intake agent needs their dispatch process. Evidence: site and forms inspected directly, but the Google profile and reviews could not be confirmed.
